title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono visit the Dakota Building in New York City | 1973
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono visited the Dakota Building in Manhattan, New York City, for the first time on 2 April 1973.

At the time they were staying in a rented home in California, but returned to New York early in the morning to conduct a 10am press conference at the Association of the Bar of the City of New York. There they announced their appeal against a deportation order which required Lennon to leave the US within 60 days. They also used the event to announce the conceptual country Nutopia.

Afterwards they were photographed in Central Park by Bob Gruen, before the viewing of apartment 72 at the Dakota, which they were interested in renting from actor Robert Ryan. They moved into the property in May 1973, and purchased the apartment later in the year.

Afterwards they returned to 105 Bank Street, their NY base since November 1971. There they gave an interview to Stuart Werbin from Rolling Stone, before taking a late-night flight back to Los Angeles.
